title: 2018 AMC 12B 15
statement: How many \(3\)-digit positive odd multiples of \(3\) do not include the digit \(3?\)

solutions.text:
Write the number as \(\overline{abc}.\) The hundreds digit \(a\) has \(8\) choices (\(1,2,4,5,6,7,8,9\)), and the units digit \(c\) has \(4\) choices (\(1,5,7,9\)).

The tens digit \(b\) may be any of \(\{0,1,2,4,5,6,7,8,9\}.\) These split into three residue classes mod \(3\) of equal size \(\{0,6,9\},\{1,4,7\},\{2,5,8\},\) so exactly \(3\) choices of \(b\) make \(a+b+c\) divisible by \(3.\)

The count is \(8\cdot4\cdot3=96.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Choose the hundreds digit (not \(0\) or \(3\)) and the units digit (odd, not \(3\)) first
For each such pair, the allowed tens digits split evenly into three residue classes mod \(3\)
